channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Rejeição a Messias revolta Lula e desespera Planalto, que culpa Alcolumbre
item.description: The Senate's rejection of Jorge Messias' nomination to the STF caused a major stir at the Planalto, which blames Senate President Davi Alcolumbre and the opposition for the defeat. Lula expressed dissatisfaction, while the government seeks to downplay the political fallout.

item.title: Senado rejeita indicação de Messias para o STF em dura derrota para o governo
item.description: The Senate rejected the nomination of Jorge Messias, Attorney General of the Union, to the Supreme Federal Court, marking a defeat for President Lula's government. The vote took place on Wednesday, April 29, in Brasília. The decision constitutes a significant setback for the Executive's agenda of STF appointments.

item.title: Governo Lula considera relação com Alcolumbre rompida de forma definitiva
item.description: The Lula government considers its relationship with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre to be definitively broken after his defeat in the effort to approve Jorge Messias for the STF. Alcolumbre's decision to block the nomination caused significant institutional strain and was seen as a direct act of opposition to the Executive. This breakdown in trust could negatively affect the government's legislative agenda in 2026.

item.title: Messias rejeitado: quantos votos no Senado receberam os 10 ministros do STF
item.description: The Senate rejected Jorge Messias' nomination to the Supreme Federal Court, securing only 34 favorable votes against 42 opposed, falling short of the 41 required. This marks the first rejection of a presidential nominee to the STF since 1894. The article also details the vote counts obtained by the ten current STF ministers during their confirmation hearings.

item.title: Rejeição de Messias pelo Senado é criticada pelo governo; vitória é 'aliança entre bolsonarismo e chantagem política', diz Boulos
item.description: Minister Guilherme Boulos criticized the Senate's rejection of Jorge Messias' nomination to the STF, calling it an 'alliance between Bolsonarism and political blackmail'. He said the Senate emerged 'smaller' from the lamentable episode.

item.title: Messias é o primeiro indicado ao STF a ser rejeitado pelo Senado desde 1894
item.description: Jorge Rodrigo Araújo Messias, the Union's Attorney General, was rejected by the Senate in a historic vote with 34 in favor and 42 against, becoming the first STF nominee blocked since 1894. The defeat occurred despite government efforts to secure the required 41 votes, reflecting resistance led by Senate President Davi Alcolumbre and an increasingly polarized climate surrounding Supreme Court nominations.

item.title: Aprovadas em Plenário cinco indicações para o CNJ
item.description: Five nominations for the National Council of Justice (CNJ) were approved in Plenary on Wednesday (29), with mandates for the 2026-2028 biennium. The approved candidates include Ilan Presser (STJ), Andréa Cunha Esmeraldo (STJ), Kátia Magalhães Arruda (TST) and two others not detailed in the provided excerpt. Voting showed strong support, with Ilan Presser receiving 61 favorable votes, Andréa Cunha Esmeraldo 60 and Kátia Magalhães Arruda 62.

item.title: Derrota histórica de Messias: Senado não rejeitava indicação ao STF desde 1894
item.description: The Senate rejected the nomination of Jorge Messias to the STF, marking the first presidential nomination rejection to the Supreme Court since 1894, during the government of Floriano Peixoto. This is the sixth such rejection in Brazilian republican history, all prior ones occurring under Peixoto’s presidency. Despite the setback, Lula retains the right to nominate another candidate or resubmit Messias, contingent on political negotiations in Congress.

item.title: Indicação de Jorge Messias ao STF é rejeitada pelo Senado
item.description: The Senate rejected Jorge Messias' nomination to the Supreme Federal Court by a vote of 42 against and 34 in favor, falling short of the 41 votes required for approval. This marks the first rejection of an STF nomination in 132 years, since the government of Floriano Peixoto in 1894. Messias, nominated by Lula to replace Luís Roberto Barroso, had his formal nomination message sent only in April, despite the announcement in November 2025.

item.title: Saiba o que acontece depois de rejeição de Messias no Senado
item.description: The Senate rejected Jorge Messias' nomination to the Supreme Federal Court, securing only 34 votes against the required 41, marking the biggest political defeat of Lula's third term. The secret vote exposed betrayals within the government's base, despite a R$13 billion investment in budget amendments. Lula must now submit a new nominee, increasing the Senate president's bargaining power.

item.title: VÍDEO mostra comemoração da oposição no Senado após rejeição de Jorge Messias para o STF
item.description: The Federal Senate rejected Jorge Messias' nomination to the Supreme Federal Court (STF) in a secret vote of 42 to 34, with one abstention. This marks the first time since 1894 that senators have rejected a presidential nominee to the STF. Opposition senators celebrated the outcome, and President Lula will now need to submit a new candidate for the vacancy left by Luis Roberto Barroso.

item.title: Senado rejeita nome de Messias para o STF, com 42 votos contrários, em derrota histórica de Lula
item.description: The Federal Senate rejected Jorge Messias' nomination to the Supreme Federal Court, with 42 votes against and 34 in favor, falling short of the 41 required. This marks the first presidential nomination rejection for the STF since 1894, under President Floriano Peixoto. The vote highlighted growing tensions between the Executive and Legislative branches, with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre openly opposing the nomination and favoring Rodrigo Pacheco.

item.title: Messias é rejeitado pelo Senado com 42 votos contra a indicação; relembre outros placares
item.description: The nomination of Jorge Messias to the Supreme Federal Court (STF) was rejected by the Senate with 42 votes against and 34 in favor, falling short of the 41 required for approval. This marks the first defeat of a Lula nominee to the STF, following over five months of delay and intense political maneuvering. The secret vote, held after the hearing, highlighted growing tensions between the government and Senate President Davi Alcolumbre.

item.title: Papo Antagonista: Messias é aprovado na CCJ e votação vai ao plenário
item.description: The Senate's Constitution and Justice Committee approved Jorge Messias's nomination to the Supreme Federal Court by a vote of 16 to 11, following an eight-hour hearing. The nomination now proceeds to a floor vote in the full Senate.

item.title: O que acontece após a rejeição de Jorge Messias no Senado?
item.description: The Senate rejected Jorge Messias' nomination to the Supreme Federal Court with 42 votes against, 34 in favor, and one abstention, despite his approval in the CCJ. The Constitution requires an absolute majority (41 votes) for approval, which was not met. President Lula must now nominate another candidate for the vacancy left by Luís Roberto Barroso.

item.title: Em rejeição histórica, Senado barra a indicação de Jorge Messias para o STF
item.description: The Senate rejected Jorge Messias' nomination to the Supreme Federal Court, with 34 votes in favor and 42 against, falling short of the 41 required. Nominated by Lula in November 2025, the appointment faced political resistance, delays, and failed government lobbying, including opposition from Senate President Davi Alcolumbre. During the CCJ hearing, Messias advocated for a more restrained STF aligned with rules, stressing judicial ethics and the need for Court improvement.

item.title: Senado rejeita Messias no STF e impõe derrota histórica a Lula
item.description: The Senate rejected Jorge Messias' nomination to the Supreme Federal Court with 42 votes against and 34 in favor, marking the first presidential nomination rejection for the STF since 1894 and constituting a historic setback for Lula in an election year. The decision exposed divisions within the government and Congress, particularly after Senate President Davi Alcolumbre supported the rejection despite Messias' prior backing. The 160-day delay between nomination and hearing — the longest since redemocratization — fueled political wear and tear and heightened politicization of the process.

item.title: Messias barrado no STF: como foi a última vez em que o Senado vetou a indicação de um ministro, ainda no século 19
item.description: The last time the Senate rejected a presidential nominee to the STF was on November 17, 1894, when Francisco Raymundo Ewerton Quadros and Demosthenes da Silveira Lobo were blocked — the last such rejection until Jorge Messias in 2024. Ewerton Quadros was rejected for lacking notable legal expertise, while Demosthenes Lobo faced serious political accusations in a secret session. Messias received 16 votes in favor and 11 against in the CCJ, tying Gilmar Mendes as the nominee with the highest historical resistance to STF confirmation.

item.title: Do IOF à dosimetria: rejeição a Messias no STF engrossa lista de derrotas marcantes de Lula 3 no Congresso
item.description: The Senate's rejection of Jorge Messias' nomination to the Supreme Federal Court (STF) marks another significant defeat for President Lula's third term in Congress, heightening tensions less than six months before the 2026 elections. This setback follows other major defeats, including the congressional overturning of the IOF tax increase in June 2023 and the approval of the Dosimetry Bill, which reduces penalties for those involved in the January 8 attacks, despite Lula's veto. Congress also overturned 56 presidential vetoes on environmental licensing in November 2023, strengthening the ruralist bloc.

item.title: Senado rejeita indicação de Jorge Messias ao STF
item.description: The Senate rejected Jorge Messias's nomination to the Supreme Federal Court (STF), with 42 votes against and 34 in favor, despite prior approval in the Constitution and Justice Committee (CCJ) by 16 to 11. Messias, a federal prosecutor nominated by President Lula, emphasized the need for balance in the Court, opposing both judicial activism and passivity, and affirmed his commitment to state secularity despite being evangelical. His nomination had already faced opposition from parties like PL and Novo, which had declared their stance against him before the hearing.

item.title: Senado rejeita indicação de Jorge Messias ao cargo de ministro do STF
item.description: The Senate plenary rejected the nomination of Jorge Messias, Attorney General of the Union, for a seat on the Supreme Federal Court, with 42 votes against and 34 in favor, in a secret vote. Messias followed the proceedings from the office of Senator Weverton Rocha (PDT-MA), who served as the rapporteur for the nomination.

item.title: Senado rejeita Messias e impõe derrota histórica ao governo Lula
item.description: The Federal Senate rejected the nomination of Jorge Messias, Attorney General of the Union, to the Supreme Federal Court, securing only 34 votes against the required 41. This marks the largest legislative defeat for President Lula’s administration in his third term, highlighting ongoing tensions between the executive and Congress. A total of 42 senators voted against the nomination.

item.title: Senado rejeita nome ao STF após 132 anos, impõe derrota histórica a Lula e barra indicação de Messias à Corte
item.description: The Senate rejected the nomination of Jorge Messias (Attorney General) to the Supreme Federal Court, with 42 votes against and 34 in favor, falling short of the 41 required for approval. This marks the first rejection of a Supreme Court nominee in Brazil's redemocratization, ending a 132-year streak since 1894, and constitutes a historic defeat for President Lula. Senate President Davi Alcolumbre is accused by Lula’s allies of orchestrating the opposition after distancing himself from the government and criticizing Messias’ nomination in favor of his own ally, Rodrigo Pacheco.

item.title: Câmara acelera projeto que reduz impostos sobre combustíveis
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies approved the urgency of a bill to reduce federal taxes on fuels such as gasoline and ethanol, aiming to counter price increases driven by the Middle East war. Proposed by government leader Paulo Pimenta (PT-RS), the measure will be voted directly in plenary, bypassing committees, with swift processing promised by Chamber President Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB). The government seeks to ease inflationary pressure on President Lula’s popularity ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Em derrota histórica, Senado rejeita indicação de Jorge Messias para o STF
item.description: The Senate rejected Jorge Messias' nomination to the Supreme Federal Court by a vote of 42 to 34, with one abstention — the first presidential nomination to the STF rejected since 1894. The vote was secret, following approval in the Constitution and Justice Committee. Messias, who had previously been questioned, opposed abortion and criticized judicial activism. President Lula must now submit a new nominee for the vacancy left by Luis Roberto Barroso.

item.title: Alcolumbre passa outras votações na frente de Messias
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre decided to vote on other appointments (CNMP, CNJ, TST) before the STF nomination of Jorge Messias, citing the Lula government's four-month delay in formalizing the nomination announced in November 2025. He aims to secure a quorum of 65 senators before voting on Messias, criticizing the late submission of documents. The CCJ approved Messias with 16 in favor and 11 against on Wednesday, April 29, 2026.

item.title: MDB reforça apoio e governistas celebram aprovação de Messias na CCJ
item.description: The MDB reinforced its support for Jorge Messias' nomination to the Supreme Federal Court, with government senators celebrating the CCJ approval by a 16-11 vote. Senate MDB leader Eduardo Braga (AM) and Senator Renan Calheiros (AL) confirmed the party's favorable vote, while rapporteur Weverton Rocha (PDT-MA) estimates 45 favorable votes in the plenary, though acknowledging greater difficulty in the final vote.

item.title: Plenário aprova indicados ao Conselho Nacional do Ministério Público
item.description: The Senate approved the nominations of Márcio Barra Lima and Carl Olav Smith for the National Council of the Public Ministry (CNMP) in a secret plenary vote. Barra Lima received 61 favorable votes, 4 against, and one abstention; Smith obtained 58 favorable, 5 against, and one abstention. Both were unanimously approved in the CCJ and will serve until 2028, overseeing the administrative, financial, and disciplinary oversight of the Public Ministry.

item.title: Zema pede mudanças na indicação de ministros do STF para evitar pessoas sem qualificação
item.description: Presidential pre-candidate Romeu Zema (Novo) advocated for changes in the appointment of STF ministers during a lunch on Wednesday (29), arguing that the current process allows the nomination of unqualified individuals. He positioned confrontation with the Supreme Court as a central pillar of his campaign, citing the court's image crisis as justification for the proposed reform.

item.title: Ao vivo: Senado vota indicação de Jorge Messias para vaga no STF
item.description: The Senate approved the nomination of Jorge Messias, Attorney General of the Union, to a seat on the Supreme Federal Court, with 16 votes in favor and 11 against. Messias underwent an 8-hour hearing by the Constitution and Justice Committee and was nominated by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva to replace the retiring Justice Roberto Barroso.

item.title: Alessandro Vieira antecipa voto favorável a Jorge Messias no STF e é elogiado por grupo Prerrogativas
item.description: Senator Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE) announced his favorable vote for Attorney General Jorge Messias during the CCJ Senate hearing for the STF ministerial vacancy. His stance was praised by the Prerrogativas group, which highlighted his consistency and commitment to judicial independence. The statement was made on April 29, 2026, pre-emptively supporting the government's nominee.

item.title: Plano de transição energética prevê ações para ampliar baterias e biocombustíveis até 2029
item.description: The National Energy Transition Plan (PNTE) of the Lula government outlines measures to be implemented by 2029 to expand the use of batteries and biofuels, aiming to increase renewable energy participation and reduce greenhouse gas emissions. The plan seeks to accelerate the decarbonization of Brazil’s energy matrix with clear medium-term targets.

item.title: Ruas pressiona STF sobre eleição-tampão no Rio: “Nada contra o desembargador”
item.description: Rio de Janeiro State Assembly President Douglas Ruas (PL) urged the STF to speed up the definition of the 'buffer election' model for the state's executive, stating he has nothing against Judge Ricardo Couto but questioning the legitimacy of decisions made by unelected officials.

item.title: Lula atrasa indicações e Copom faz sua 3ª reunião seguida desfalcado
item.description: President Lula delayed appointments to two vacancies at the Central Bank, leaving the Copom with reduced quorum for three consecutive meetings. On April 29, 2026, the committee cut the Selic rate by 0.25 percentage points, totaling a 0.5 p.p. reduction for the year, despite all seven current directors having voted to raise the rate to 15% in June 2025. The open positions are for the Director of Financial System Organization and Resolution and Director of Economic Policy, with names like Guilherme Mello considered but not nominated.

item.title: Banco Central corta Selic em 0,25 p.p. e taxa cai para 14,50%
item.description: The Central Bank cut the Selic rate by 0.25 percentage points to 14.50%, marking the second consecutive reduction and a total of 0.50 p.p. decline in 2026. The decision, widely expected and unanimous, came despite inflation above target and forecasts of 4.86% for the year, driven by Middle East war impacts on oil, diesel, gasoline, and freight costs. The Copom meeting proceeded with a reduced quorum due to two unfilled director positions pending presidential appointment.

item.title: Com receio de derrota, Lula questiona líder do governo sobre cenário de aprovação de Messias no Senado
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva questioned government leader Jaques Wagner about the Senate approval of Jorge Messias for the Supreme Court, expressing concern over a possible unprecedented defeat following actions by Senate President Davi Alcolumbre against the nomination. Although approved in the CCJ by a 16-11 vote, Messias faces a secret plenary vote requiring at least 41 votes, with the government expecting support from around 45 senators. During the hearing, Messias advocated for STF reforms, condemned abortion, and praised God, signaling to the opposition to gain their support.

item.title: PF diz que Monark questiona a lisura das eleições; Moraes pede parecer da PGR
item.description: The Federal Police is investigating influencer Monark for alleged disobedience to court rulings, stating he repeatedly questions the legitimacy of Brazilian elections, electronic voting machines, and the actions of the TSE and STF. Minister Alexandre de Moraes has given the PGR a 15-day deadline to comment on the PF’s report, following the analysis of TikTok-provided files. The investigation, launched after the January 8, 2023 attacks, has seen deadlines extended due to technical limitations in data extraction.

item.title: Lula liberou mais R$ 270 mi em emendas e movimentou Senado por Messias
item.description: Lula's government allocated R$ 270 million in parliamentary amendments on April 28, one day before Jorge Messias' STF nomination hearing, raising the annual total to R$ 13 billion. The effort, led by Institutional Relations Minister José Guimarães and Senator Randolfe Rodrigues, aimed to secure Senate approval for Messias after overcoming initial resistance from Senate President Davi Alcolumbre, who now publicly supports the nomination.

item.title: Senador que propôs indiciar ministros do STF em relatório de CPI declara voto em Messias
item.description: Senator Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE) declared his vote for Union Attorney General Jorge Messias to fill a Supreme Court vacancy during a CCJ session. Vieira was the author of the final report of the Organized Crime CPI that proposed indicting Supreme Court ministers, including Dias Toffoli, Alexandre de Moraes, and Gilmar Mendes, and received solidarity after being targeted by the justices. CCJ President Otto Alencar and government leader Randolfe Rodrigues defended his parliamentary immunity.

item.title: O balde de água fria do relator da PEC do fim da escala 6×1 na oposição de Lula
item.description: Leo Prates, the rapporteur of the PEC to end the 6×1 work scale, rejected demands for financial or tax compensation to the productive sector, stating that Brazil has already granted fiscal remissions without societal benefit and that the proposal should be approved without such concessions. He emphasized his focus on creating productive arrangements to improve workers' lives and his commitment to the timeline set by the Chamber president to approve the PEC by the end of May. The opposition seeks to delay the debate by demanding compensation for businesses, but Prates has signaled he will not yield to this pressure.

item.title: ‘Não é o crime que é organizado, os estados é que ainda não são’, diz secretário nacional de Segurança
item.description: National Public Security Secretary Chico Lucas stated that organized crime is not the issue—rather, the states' lack of organization is. At a JOTA event in Brasília, experts emphasized the need for dialogue between public security, revenue agencies, and regulators to combat the illegal economy, which is expanding due to new technologies and economic flows. The discussion, part of the 'Economia Legal' coverage during an election year, focused on how violence distorts markets and undermines public policy formulation.

item.title: Ruas sobe o tom, cobra rapidez do STF e diz que quem governa ‘de forma interina carece de legitimidade’
item.description: Douglas Ruas (PL), president of the Rio de Janeiro State Legislature (Alerj), criticized the continued appointment of Judge Ricardo Couto as interim governor, arguing he lacks legitimacy and urging the STF to rule swiftly. He advocated for direct elections to fill the remainder of the term, condemned the interim government's mass dismissals (859 since March 24), and claimed he is being targeted by a 'political gymnasium' orchestrated by Eduardo Paes (PSD).

item.title: Vieira declara voto favorável à indicação de Messias ao STF
item.description: Senator Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE) stated he would vote in favor of Jorge Messias, the Attorney General of the Union, for a seat on the Supreme Federal Court (STF), describing the vote as 'a social media success' and 'a preventive impeachment' against STF ministers. During the hearing, Vieira questioned whether Messias possesses the 'moral stature and courage' needed to confront fellow justices on the court.

item.title: Enquanto finaliza pacote de crédito, governo acelera fortemente o gasto e tenta recuperar popularidade
item.description: The Lula government accelerated public spending in early 2025, driven by the advance payment of R$ 68 billion in court rulings, aiming to boost popularity ahead of the 2026 elections. This fiscal stimulus comes as the government's credit package is still being finalized. The move reflects an effort to counter declining popularity through increased public expenditure.

item.title: Advogada de Bolsonaro fez campanha para Messias
item.description: Karina Kufa, lawyer representing Jair and Eduardo Bolsonaro in older legal cases, campaigned in recent days for the approval of Jorge Messias' nomination to the STF in the Senate, having been present since early morning at the CCJ to follow his hearing. The exclusive article highlights the involvement of Bolsonaro-aligned legal figures in the political maneuvering around the Supreme Court appointment.

item.title: 'Tarcísio não é imbatível', 'mero recall' e 'palanque forte': o que disseram os pré-candidatos a governo e Senado sobre a pesquisa Quaest em SP
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows Tarcísio de Freitas leading with 38% in the first round, followed by Fernando Haddad at 26%, though his government approval dropped from 60% to 54% over eight months. Kim Kataguiri and Paulo Serra each have 5%, with Kataguiri noting strong youth support tied to MBL. No campaign is fully satisfied: Tarcísio downplayed the results, Haddad remained silent, but his coordinator said he is not unbeatable and will grow.

item.title: Câmara instala comissão do fim da escala 6×1 e mira votação ainda em maio
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies installed a special committee to analyze a PEC proposing the end of the 6×1 work scale and a reduction of the weekly workweek from 44 to 36 hours, potentially enabling a four-day workweek. The committee, chaired by Alencar Santana (PT-SP) with rapporteur Leo Prates (Republicanos-BA), comprises 38 members and aims to vote on the text by the end of May, under pressure from Lula’s urgent constitutional bill on the same issue.

item.title: Messias defende oposição em sabatina: “Só existe na democracia”
item.description: President Lula’s nominee to the Supreme Federal Court, Jorge Messias, stated during his Senate CCJ hearing that opposition only exists in democracies and that the STF must safeguard parliamentary prerogatives, even when rulings counteract the government. He emphasized that the Court must defend the political opposition to the Planalto to ensure a living democracy, particularly regarding the Organized Crime CPI and the INSS CPMI. If approved in the CCJ, the vote will proceed directly to the plenary session later this Wednesday.

item.title: Wagner deixa sabatina de Messias e encontra Lula com Jerônimo
item.description: Senate government leader Jaques Wagner met with President Lula at the Palácio da Alvorada while Jorge Messias's confirmation hearing took place in the Senate's Constitution and Justice Committee. Shortly after, Bahia Governor Jerônimo Rodrigues also arrived at the official residence. On the same day, Jerônimo appears technically tied with ACM Neto in an electoral poll released that day.

item.title: O novo balanço do STF sobre os condenados por participação em atos golpistas
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes released a report showing that 1,402 defendants have been held responsible for the January 8, 2023, coup attempts, representing 75% of the 1,878 individuals denounced by the Prosecutor General's Office. Additionally, 552 cases were resolved through non-prosecution agreements, and 169 definitive prison sentences have been issued, including 55 under house arrest and 111 in closed regime, with penalties reaching up to 27 years and three months.
